Neither of the options given is correct: a muscle fibre relaxes when calcium ions are pumped back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum, so troponin-tropomyosin blocks the myosin-binding sites on actin and cross-bridge cycling stops. Running out of oxygen impairs contraction rather than triggering relaxation, and a forceful nerve stimulus increases rather than shuts down contraction. Relaxation is thus a calcium-dependent, active reuptake process followed by passive lengthening.
CONFIDENCE: 92
